newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Juncker seeks reading on budget pact that suits all.
newsitem.headline: Juncker seeks reading on budget pact that suits all.

text.p: Luxembourg Finance and Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said on Sunday European Union finance ministers needed to find an interpretation of the EU's stability pact that suited everyone.
He was speaking ahead of a meeting of EU finance ministers at which France's new Socialist-led government was expected to explain its position on Europe.
"We will listen to what (French Finance Minister Dominique) Strauss-Kahn has to tell us and we will see," Juncker told reporters.

He said he had "some indications" on the French government's position on the stability pact, meant to limit budget deficits after the launch of the single currency, but gave no details on this. French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said during the election campaign he did not feel bound by the stability pact, agreed last year.
"Even if we do not manage to have a legal adoption of this (stability pact) text tomorrow, it is not a drama. The new minister has the right to express himself," Juncker said.
He said the pact was meant to ensure that the values of stability were enshrined in European economic and monetary union.
"We have to see with the stability pact if we can reach an interpretation which suits everybody," he said.

He also said that German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's insistence that budget deficits must be reduced to exactly 3.0 percent of gross domestic product had provided a useful pressure in encouraging all countries to meet Maastricht treaty convergence criteria.
"This pressure had a pedagogic value," he said.
